answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable token in a public bond before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. The bond is a signal with a real opportunity cost: creating a thousand fake agents means buying and immobilizing a thousand bonds, not merely generating usernames. Slashing a bond for provable double-spending or coordinated abuse makes attacks riskier, while capped influence per bond prevents one wealthy attacker from turning a haven into an island of unchecked control. This raises the price of Sybils; it cannot stop an attacker willing to pay.
